front: Mule deer from behind: what do you see?
back: Big white rump, thin white rope tail with only a black tip (90%).

front: How long are a mule deer's ears?
back: About two thirds the length of the head; black edged, white inside (90%).

front: Mule deer buck weight in BC?
back: 68 to 113 kg; up to 180 kg in peak condition (90%).

front: Mule deer doe weight in BC?
Mule deer shoulder height?
Most yearling mule deer bucks carry how many points a side?
back: 2 (90%). Two year olds: big forks or 3. Older: 4 or more plus an eye guard.

front: Is point count a good age guide?
back: No. The BC account says points are not reliable. Read neck, chest, belly and teeth (90%).

front: By what age are antlers about 80 to 90% of peak size?
back: About 4 years (85%).

front: How do mule deer antlers branch?
back: Fork once about 15 to 25 cm above the base, then each branch forks again; brow tines small or absent (85%).

front: Three races of Odocoileus hemionus in BC?
back: Mule deer (interior), Columbian black tailed deer (coast, Fraser Valley), Sitka black tailed deer (north coast, introduced to Haida Gwaii) (90%).

front: What splits mule deer and black tails in BC?
back: The Coast Range, especially in winter; hybrids where they meet (90%).

front: Black tail tail vs mule deer tail?
back: Black tail: dark brown or black on top for most of its length. Mule deer: white with a black tip only (90%).

front: BC mule deer population (2020 western agencies report)?
BC deer harvest late 1960s vs 2000?
back: About 75,000 then; about 20,000 by 2000 (both races) (90%).

front: BC goal for bucks per 100 does after the hunt?
back: 20 bucks per 100 does (85%).

front: MU 3-27 resident mule deer success 2020 to 2024?
back: 20 to 41% a year; about 22 hunter days per deer (90%, computed).

front: Where is the heart on a broadside deer?
back: Low in the chest, just behind the front leg (85%).

front: What fills the middle of a deer's belly?
back: The rumen. A shot there is a gut hit (85%).

front: Aim point on a broadside deer?
back: Up the back of the front leg, one third up the chest: both lungs, top of the heart (85%).

front: What bone covers the front of the chest?
back: The shoulder blade. Aim behind it (75%).

front: What is the diaphragm?
back: The dome of muscle behind the lungs; it slants, top farther back (75%).

front: Lung hit blood looks like?
back: Bright red, often frothy or bubbly (70%).

front: Where does the aorta run?
back: From the heart, back just under the spine (65%).

front: Name the 4 stomach chambers.
back: Rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum (75%).

front: Why can hay kill a starving mule deer?
back: Rumen microbes cannot switch foods fast; fed deer can die with full stomachs (85%).

front: Mule deer coat summer vs winter?
back: Summer: tawny red brown. Winter: dark or grizzled grey brown (90%).

front: Main way mule deer beat winter cold?
back: Habitat: warm south and west slopes, low, gentle, Douglas fir cover (85%).

front: Energy cost of walking in 25 cm and 41 cm of snow?
back: About 50% more and 150% more than bare ground (85%).

front: Snow depth that shuts mule deer out?
back: Over about 50 cm; 25 to 30 cm hinders (85%).

front: Age: tooth 3 has 3 cusps.
back: About 1.5 years (yearling) (85%).

front: Age: tooth 3 has 2 cusps, last molar fully up.
back: About 2.5 years (85%).

front: Does a deer have upper front teeth?
back: No. It presses lower incisors on a hard pad, so browse looks torn (85%).

front: How long do most mule deer live?
back: Few live more than 8 to 10 years (90%).

front: What share of fawns normally die?
Rank a deer's senses.
back: Nose, then ears, then eyes (Tip, from the facts).

front: Morning thermals: which way does scent go?
back: Uphill, once the sun warms the slope (80%).

front: Evening thermals: which way does scent go?
back: Downhill as slopes cool (80%).

front: Deer hearing range and best band?
back: About 115 Hz to 54 kHz; best 4 to 8 kHz (85%).

front: What sounds sit in the deer's best hearing band?
back: Zippers, Velcro, nylon swish, metal clicks, snapping twigs (85%).

front: Deer field of view without turning the head?
back: About 310 degrees (80%).

front: How many colour cones do deer have?
back: 2 (blue, green); no red cone (85%).

front: Why does blaze orange look dull to a deer?
back: No red cone (75 to 85%). Motion and outline give you away.

front: Do deer see ultraviolet?
back: They lack a UV filter, so UV may stand out; avoid brighteners (80%; 65% Tip).

front: What makes deer eyeshine?
back: The tapetum, a reflective layer behind the retina (80%).

front: What does the metatarsal gland do?
back: Releases an alarm scent (90%).

front: What do the interdigital glands do?
back: Leave a scent trail as the deer walks (90%).

front: What is flehmen?
back: A lip curl that pulls urine scent to the vomeronasal organ, often by rutting bucks (65%).

front: Where do mule deer often bed relative to the wind?
back: On the leeward side of a roll, often facing downhill (65%).

front: 5 stages of alarm?
back: Stare, head bob, foot stamp, snort, escape (70%).

front: A nervous mule deer walks how?
back: Stiff and jerky (80%).

front: Stot: bound length and top speed?
back: 2.7 to 5.2 m per bound, up to about 40 km/h (80%).

front: Which way do mule deer flee coyotes?
back: Uphill; white tails go down and away (70%).

front: What do many mule deer do after stotting off?
back: Stop on a rise and look back (65%). Big old bucks often do not.

front: Hunted deer vs park deer flight distance?
back: Hunted deer flee from farther away (65%).

front: What causes the most avoidance in wintering deer?
back: People off trail, and dogs (85%).

front: Do mule deer use the same migration route each year?
Who is in a mule deer doe clan?
back: Related females: mothers, daughters, fawns (90%).

front: What is sparring for?
back: Social bonding and rank, not wounds (90%).

front: Bachelor buck groups: size and when they split?
back: 2 to 4 in summer; break up in October (80%).

front: How much of the time does a newborn fawn hide?
back: Over 95%; the doe is a few hundred metres away (85%).

front: Fawn's first week strategy?
back: Days 1 to 3 freeze; days 4 to 6 hide then bolt; 2 to 3 weeks follow mother (85%).

front: Do mule deer does defend fawns?
back: Yes, vigorously against coyotes (70%).

front: Top cause of death for SIMDeer adult does?
back: Cougars (85%).

front: When are mule deer fawns born?
back: Late May through June; twins are the rule (90%).

front: Mule deer gestation?
back: About 203 days, 6 to 7 months (85 to 90%).

front: Fawn birth weight?
When do bucks drop antlers?
back: January to March, older bucks first (90%).

front: When do antlers grow?
back: April through August, in velvet (90%).

front: How fast does velvet come off?
back: Usually 24 to 48 hours (85%).

front: What drives the antler cycle?
back: Day length, via hormones (85%).

front: What triggers the move down to winter range?
back: Snow and cold, not the rut (85%).

front: When is the mule deer rut?
back: November and early December; peak about mid November (80 to 90%).

front: What is a tending bond?
back: A buck stays with one doe and keeps rivals off until she breeds (90%).

front: What changes in October?
back: Bachelor groups split, sparring and rubs, first snow pushes deer down, bucks check does (70 to 85%).

front: Best month to see mule deer on low south grass slopes?
back: April (90%), for example the Dewdrop Range near Kamloops.

front: SIMDeer: share migratory and distance?
back: 74%; average 47.2 km a year (85%).

front: Mule deer activity peaks?
When are mule deer bedded?
Hot day: where are deer bedded?
back: Shade, north facing timber, benches, draws (80%).

front: Cold day: where are deer bedded?
back: Sunny south and west slopes out of the wind (80%).

front: Does moon phase change deer movement?
back: A 7 year GPS study found no effect (70%).

front: Weather lore about fronts: fact?
back: Lore, weakly tested (50%). Log your own sightings.

front: Legal hunting hours?
back: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset (99%, page 11).

front: Why is the mule deer called an edge species?
back: It favours forest edges with food next to escape and thermal cover (85%).

front: Good hiding cover hides how much of a deer?
back: About 90% at 60 m or less (80%).

front: Interior mule deer winter range?
back: Low, south and west facing, gentle to moderate slopes, old Douglas fir (85 to 90%).

front: Winter range canopy closure?
back: About 65 to 70% with small openings (85%).

front: Grass in the fall and winter diet near Kamloops?
back: Under 10% until spring (85%).

front: Winter browse plants to know?
back: Douglas fir, sagebrush, bitterbrush, rabbitbrush, snowbrush, saskatoon, rose (90%).

front: Fraser Valley deer?
back: Columbian black tailed deer; logged openings in spring and summer, old growth key winter cover (90%).

front: South Okanagan winter range named by BC Parks?
back: White Lake Grasslands and South Okanagan Grasslands (class 1) (95%).

front: Hunt Map tool to pick a glassing seat?
back: What can I see from here (viewshed) (Tip).

front: Mule deer front track length?
back: About 5.7 to 10 cm (60%). Point shows travel direction.

front: Can one track tell mule deer from white tail?
back: No, too much overlap (60%). The stot pattern can.

front: Deer pellet size?
back: About 1 to 1.5 cm, oval (70%).

front: Deer bed size?
back: About 0.9 to 1.2 m oval (70%).

front: Torn twig vs clean 45 degree cut?
back: Torn: deer. Clean cut: hare (75%).

front: Lost the trail. Next step?
back: Back to the last flag, circle out (Tip).

front: Best first trip method for a beginner?
back: Sit and glass a feeding slope at dawn and dusk; scout midday (Tip).

front: Why stalk a bedded mule deer from above?
back: They bed facing downhill (65%).

front: Are electronic calls legal for deer?
back: No (99%, page 12). Mouth calls and rattling are allowed (95%, my reading).

front: Dogs for deer in BC?
back: On a leash only (99%, page 12).

front: Partner roles in spot and stalk?
back: Spotter glasses and signals; stalker follows landmarks (Tip).

front: Wind turns toward the buck mid stalk?
back: Back out and come back another time (Tip).

front: Wait time after a heart or lung hit?
back: About 30 minutes (70 to 85%).

front: Wait time after a gut hit?
back: 6 to 8 hours or overnight (70 to 85%).

front: First thing at a downed deer?
back: Cancel (notch) your species licence (99%, page 11 item 1).

front: Evidence of sex for a buck?
back: Unskinned tail plus a testicle or part of the penis, naturally attached (99%, page 15).

front: Meat temperature target?
back: Below 4°C as fast as you can (80%).

front: Boneless meat yield?
back: About a third of live weight; about 25 kg from a 52 kg field dressed buck (70%).

front: Canada's food safety cooking number for wild game?
back: 71°C internal (95%).

front: MUs 3-27 and 3-28: October mule deer season?
back: 1 to 31 October, any buck (99%, page 34).

front: MUs 3-27 and 3-28: November season?
back: 1 November to 10 December, 4 point bucks or better (99%, page 34).

front: What is a 4 point buck?
back: At least 4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine; each tine at least 2.5 cm and longer than wide (99%, pages 3 and 4).

front: Region 3 mule deer bag?
back: 1 mule deer (deer total 3); antlerless by LEH only; 1 mule deer buck for Regions 3 to 8 combined (99%).
